sections.h2: Out-of-pocket spending stopped falling and rose again in 2022-23

chart.title: Households paid a bigger share of health costs directly in 2022-23
chart.sub: Out-of-pocket spending, % of total health expenditure.

sections.means: Households paid 43.4% of health spending directly in 2022-23, up from 39.4% a year earlier.
sections.todo: Put government health spending on the committee's time-bound path to 2.5% of GDP.

sections.h2: Households pay more per hospital stay than PM-JAY pays per admission

chart.title: Out-of-pocket cost of a hospital stay in 2025 exceeded the average PM-JAY payment
chart.sub: Rupees per hospital admission or stay.

sections.means: Households paid an average of Rs 34,064 out of pocket per hospital stay in 2025, against about Rs 15,300 paid per PM-JAY admission since 2018.
sections.todo: Extend PM-JAY to outpatient consultations, diagnostics and medicines, as the committee proposes.

sections.h2: Covering outpatient care would cost 2.1 to 4.2 times PM-JAY's hospital claims

chart.title: Outpatient cover would cost several times the Centre's PM-JAY budget
chart.sub: Rs thousand crore a year. PM-JAY figures in current rupees; outpatient figures in 2022-23 prices. Illustrative estimate, not a costing.
chart.source: PM-JAY figures; National Health Accounts 2022-23; this blog's arithmetic.
rows: PM-JAY: hospital claims a year, average since 2018

sections.means: Covering PM-JAY's eligible people for outpatient care would cost Rs 0.5 to 1.1 lakh crore a year, 2.1 to 4.2 times what PM-JAY pays for hospital care.
sections.todo: Deliver outpatient care through free medicines and tests at public facilities such as Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, rather than a claim for each visit.
